sourceInformation.source: Eye of the Beholder 1991 (Westwood Associates / SSI; MS-DOS and Amiga)
sourceInformation.genre: Real-time, first-person, grid-based party RPG dungeon crawler with lock-and-key puzzles
sourceInformation.perspective: First-person party view on a 4-way grid with tweened steps and quarter turns; top-down automap
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge 2D engine v0.85.2 (dist/handoff) and 3D engine v0.85.2 (three.js r182 and Rapier 0.19.3 from jsDelivr); AI Hub session client 1.4.0; Node 24 and Playwright 1.63.0 for tests; plain JavaScript bundled into one HTML file
sourceInformation.artDirection: The engine's native low-resolution 3D look: code-drawn walls and things, rigs drawn as pixel cards, toon light, fog, a brass lockwork UI
sourceInformation.animation: The engine's rigs and E.Blob, a tweened first-person camera with bob and bump, doors and gates that rise and swing, a pen-drawn Bolt-Holder eye with sliding bolts, drawn monster wind-ups
sourceInformation.audio: The engine's chip synth: step-sequencer songs per floor and a boss cue, synthesized sound effects, no audio files. Babble voices: a WebAudio formant synth speaks each vowel of dialogue (not checked by ear).
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1, ghost mode, 1 to 4 players on the Rat Run race (the hub's harness passes for 2 players, for 4 players with latency and loss, and for the host-leave case). Solo Rat Run: a best-run golden ghost from a 10 Hz trail kept in local storage.
sourceInformation.testing: node tests/run.mjs: lint of the maps and wiring, sim determinism and save round-trip, the walkthrough bot clearing floor 1 and reaching floor 2, the Bolt-Holder's mechanics under god mode, the AI Hub harness (three runs), and a browser check. Under normal balance the bot does not clear floor 3. Floors 3 and 4 and the Veil-refused branch were checked for mechanics under god mode only.
sourceInformation.research: Read the engine's API card, its 3D manual and the starter crawler kit; no web research
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux (WSL2); browser: headless Chromium 1243 via Playwright

testingFeedback: About twenty defects, found by the bot runs and the sim checks (estimate).

Six were critical: combat damage that never reached the counters, a key that never reached the pack, a door the bot closed behind itself, a stand cell on the far side of a door, a hand emptied before a throw, and a stall while a monster stood near.
The most helpful test was the floor-one bot trace that printed each goal change with the hand contents.
The least helpful test was the browser smoke test, which checks for errors and the first screens, not play.
engineFeedback: Most liked: the 3D world API (a fixed camera, things, mobs as cards, the pen) and the 2D engine's game.debug and input.tap / hold for tests.
Got stuck: the 3D things list has no plate or stair, so we drew them; the input presets merge with our own action names in ways the API card does not spell out.
Most important thing we built ourselves: the sim, the bot, the wiring, the dungeon presenter and every screen.
Hardest part: the input and menu details (custom action names, pause menu items, settings), which the API card only sketches.
One thing to change: ship the common things (plate, stair, a door variant) in the 3D library, and document the custom input map in one table.
promptFeedback: Most liked: the exact maps, ids and tables, which made the content checkable.
Confusing: some numbers do not follow the plan's own formulas (Durgan's HP), 'silent' teleporters are described two ways, and the plan asks for E.Grid where a small breadth-first search was simpler.
Hardest: holding every system to its full depth in one session; the spec is larger than one session.
Would change: a cut list per milestone that says what to drop first, and an acceptance list per floor.

aiHub.name: Eye of the Bolt-Holder
aiHub.description: A real-time, first-person party dungeon crawl beneath Hasp, the City of a Thousand Locks: drains, clockwork halls and eye-cults, with levers, plates and keys, spells memorized at camp, and the caged Eye that holds the city's bolts.
aiHub.controls: W/S move, Q/E turn, A/D strafe, F use, Space strike, I party, C camp, M map; pad: stick move, D-pad turn, Cross use, Square strike
